# Annotation volume geometry

## The model
- A location is stored in **mosaic** (section) space: `MosaicShape`, `X`, `Y`, `Radius`, `Width`. Mosaic is the truth. On
  the gRPC client `LocationObj.MosaicShape` and `VolumeShape` are `IShape2D` (a circle is a `Geometry.Circle`).
- `VolumeShape`, `VolumeX`, `VolumeY` (and the volume radius inside a circle's `VolumeShape`) are a **cache**: the mosaic
  geometry mapped through a section-to-volume transform. The persisted cache holds the volume's **default** transform
  (enforced in phase 3).
- A changed `.stos` must re-render every annotation at once, so nothing that draws may trust the cache.

## The forward owner: `LocationVolumeGeometry` (SqlGeometryAnnotationExtensions)
`LocationVolumeGeometry.For(location, transform)` (or `For(location, provider)`) is the only place mosaic geometry is
mapped forward for drawing. It carries:
- `Shape`: `MapShape(type, mosaic, transform)` = `GetSmoothedShape(TryMapShapeSectionToVolume(mosaic))`. The same
  function `VolumePositionUpdateJob` writes into the cache, so the cache and the views always agree.
- `ControlPoints` / `ControlPolygon()`: the mapped, unsmoothed control points (edit handles, polylines, polygons).
- `Circle` (circles, points): centre from `X,Y`, radius by the five-point mean (`circle-mapping-scale.mdc`).
- `Scale`: the local five-point mean scale. `Width` = mosaic width x `Scale`; `Radius` = mosaic radius x `Scale` (the
  circle's own radius for circles). Line and curve widths scale exactly as circle radii do.
- `Center` (labels, markers, link previews), `AdjacentMarker(scalar)` (the circle drawn on an adjacent section: the
  inscribed circle of the mapped shape for polygon-likes), `Outline` (the polygon polygon-likes are hit-tested as and
  links leave), `InterpolationPoints` (what curve views draw with, so drawn == hit-tested).

It is cached per location, keyed by the `MosaicShape` instance (the `IShape2D`, converted to SQL geometry once), width,
type and the transform **object** (a reloaded `.stos` is a new object), so a shape edit or a transform change rebuilds it.
A transform provider must therefore hand out the same object for a section until its `.stos` changes
(`VolumeViewModel`'s mappings; `VolumeTransformProvider` keeps one per section). One documented mapping-failure policy lives
on the class (circles extrapolate the centre and keep the mosaic radius; other shapes extrapolate with scale 1;
`CanDrawOnSection` is false for extrapolated polygons and polylines). Do not add a second policy in a view.

## Views
- Views (`View/`, `ViewModel/`) take a `LocationVolumeGeometry`; `AnnotationViewFactory` builds it. Views never receive or
  call a transform: no `SectionToVolume(`, `TrySectionToVolume(`, `TryMapShapeSectionToVolume(`.
- Views never read the stored cache: no `.VolumePosition`, `.VolumeShape`, `VolumeX/VolumeY` for drawing or hit-testing.
  Code with a location but no transform uses `LocationVolumeGeometryExtensions` (`VolumeGeometry()`, `VolumeCenter()`,
  `VolumeRadius()`), which reads the open volume's transforms (Jotunn's `AnnotationBootstrap.Transforms`, else Viking's
  open volume).
- A link, label or marker that belongs to a location takes its geometry from that location's owner, so it meets what is
  drawn.
- `VolumeGeometryGuardTests` enforces this for `View/` and `ViewModel/`; each exception is on its named, commented
  allow-list. `LocationVolumeGeometryTests` checks every view and every factory branch against the owner (property and
  closed-set tests); add a new view there.

## Commands and edits (phase 2 target, the inverse rule)
The user edits in volume space (what is on screen). A command maps the edited geometry **back to mosaic** with the
inverse transform (`VolumeToSection`; the five-point mean for a circle radius or a line width), saves `MosaicShape` (and
`Width`) as the truth, and writes `VolumeShape` only as `LocationVolumeGeometry.MapShape` of the new mosaic shape. A
command never copies a volume value into the mosaic columns or writes a volume shape it did not derive from mosaic. Edit
previews inside commands (translate, adjust control point, resize, retrace) are still hand-mapped until phase 2 moves them.
